author: duy90
text:
TheLastNail wrote: My actual
dilemma is how to differentiate FL from any common FTR. Do we know FTR
is FL only after that FTR bounce price in future then that bounce make
new high/low. After that we can say that FTR was indeed a FL? That seems
 very likely, as compression is PAZ and FLs are created after break of
PAZ.

FL is usually sideways move 1 - n bars which then breaks in the intended
 direction. For example high wave candle or doji on daily candle is FL
as there is indecision within that bar in ltf. Basically on lower TF in
this FL price is moved inside FL "box" and after breaking this box
creates an FTR.

FTR itself is a retracement after an engulf. You can confirm it is FTR after making HH in "uptrend"or LL "downtrend"

author: althoufx
text:
IF really thank you a lot for your quick reply !

....trying to make the puzzle:

as first any little move on the chart is made by the ITs. Retailers just jump on it.

So any swing H and L was specially made by ITs to get specific reactions
 (orders) by retailers. Obviously ITs move by imbalancing, then placing
their sells/buys against retailers + imbalance necessary for the move (i
 think).

in the upper part of the chart there are swings H & HH.

Some Retailers sell immediately below H + stop above. ITs take all stop as BUY orders.

Other Retailers buy immediately above H + stop below L. ITs take only orders, again BUY orders .

Other Retailers have here Stop of sell orders placed below the L. ITs take all as BUY orders

in the lower part of the chart there are swings L & LL

Some Retailers buy immediately above L + stop below. ITs take all stop as SELL orders

Other Retailers sell immediately below L + stop above H. ITs take only orders, SELL orders

Other Retailers have here stop of buy orders placed above H. ITs take all as SELL orders

So at the end of all cycles IT will have collected a number of closed BUY and SELL Stop Loss + orders

it means also a predominance of BUY or SELL orders, when ITs consider that amount satisfactory, they will move against it.

in that chart the predominance should be BUY retail orders, then we can expect a pole down.

It seems to be a true classic of the CP.

....I hope it is not just a mess and i've got it....

all the best
